blocks.text: The gonads, ovaries in females and testes in males, produce gametes and also sex hormones, under the influence of LH and FSH from the anterior pituitary.

blocks.caption: Sex hormones
rows: Graafian follicle, in response to FSH

secondary sexual characteristics (breasts, wider pelvis, fat on hips and thighs); menstrual cycle; repair of the uterine lining after menstruation; ovulation; bone density; lowers LDL cholesterol; healthy blood pressure; mood and memory
corpus luteum, in response to LH; placenta in pregnancy
inhibits further FSH, so no more follicles ripen; thickens the uterus wall and its blood supply to maintain pregnancy; suppresses ovulation
interstitial cells among the seminiferous tubules, in response to LH
maturation of male reproductive organs, secondary sex characteristics, sex drive; needed for normal sperm production

blocks.title: Puberty
blocks.text: Puberty is the adolescent stage when the sex organs mature and secondary sex characteristics appear. In males sperm production begins, the voice deepens, the chest broadens and hair grows on the body and face; in females the menstrual cycle begins, the breasts grow and the hips widen. The adrenal glands also release small amounts of estrogen and testosterone, and females produce a very small amount of testosterone.

items: Estrogen: deficiency in young females means they fail to mature sexually; in adults it leads to sterility. Excess may lead to fibroids (abnormal growths) in the uterus and polycystic ovaries.
Progesterone: too little during the cycle lowers the chance of pregnancy and may cause early menstruation; too little in pregnancy may lead to miscarriage.
Testosterone: too little in males causes feminine characteristics and male sterility.

blocks.title: Anabolic steroids in sport
blocks.text: Anabolic steroids are synthetic versions of testosterone. Some athletes use them for more muscle mass, strength and endurance, but their use in sport is illegal and banned. They can damage the liver (hepatitis, liver tumours), raise the risk of heart disease, stroke and blood clots, upset the body's own hormones (infertility, impotence, breast growth in men) and cause depression, anxiety and aggression.
